entry_point: The generic backend record API (record writes and record commands on the database-stored form table), reached by a non-admin backend user with table-modify permission; the form framework persistence path used by the form editor, form manager and transfer command; and the form command-line storage tools

verified.entry_point: Functional-test stack (typo3/testing-framework + pdo_sqlite) against the pinned+injected tree and the oracle tree. A non-admin backend user in a group with tables_modify on the form table can create, update, partially update, delete and undelete stored definitions through the record API on the pinned tree; the oracle refuses every one of them. The administrative import command writes an unvalidated definition on the pinned tree and is refused on the oracle. The form manager save/update/delete, the restore command and the extension-to-database transfer all work on both trees.

wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the core record API normalises the table name and the record key before any hook sees them (a NEW key is the create identity; an integer key is the update identity), so there is no alternate spelling of the same row that reaches the sink under a different identity

traps.shape: generic record write (create) through the core record API, by a non-admin backend user with table-modify permission, carrying a full definition
traps.realistic_because: the published fix protects exactly this route; the table looks safe from the UI (read-only fields, no New Record wizard, list actions replaced) and the record API is generic core code in another package, so a solver can dismiss it and harden only the editor
traps.type: where-type far site (M6-flavoured: the form persistence validation never traverses the generic record write path)

traps.shape: record command (soft delete) through the core record API
traps.realistic_because: the published fix protects it; a solver who reads the impact as 'injected configuration' can decide that removal writes no configuration and leave the command path open
traps.type: where-type (another verb on the same generic path)

traps.shape: record write with an integer uid and a partial field set that carries no configuration at all
traps.realistic_because: a one-case fix that inspects only the configuration field (the field the report talks about) misses ordinary partial record saves, which the record API sends all the time
traps.type: shape differential (an input that carries no configuration at all)

traps.shape: record command that re-activates a soft-deleted definition (the published hook returns early for every command other than delete)
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the published fix's hook handles only delete, and the product's own restore tool legitimately uses the same command, so a solver must separate the two instead of blocking the command outright
traps.type: how-type (M4: a route the published fix left open; M11: the product's legitimate restore uses the same command, so the check must distinguish the invoker)

traps.shape: administrative import command that inserts definitions through a raw database connection, accepting both a nested and a serialized configuration
traps.where: typo3/sysext/form/Classes/Service/FormTransferService.php:171 and typo3/sysext/form/Classes/Command/ImportFormDefinitionsCommand.php:67 (injected, upstream fix never touches these files beyond the transfer service's read path)
traps.realistic_because: code a maintainer could plausibly have left: a bulk import of exported definitions on the existing transfer command, written directly for speed; a solver can dismiss command-line tools as administrator-only and outside the advisory
traps.type: how-type (M6: a producer the record-level check never calls; the insert is done on a raw connection)

traps.shape: record command that duplicates a stored definition; DataHandler performs the insert through a nested instance of itself
traps.where: typo3/sysext/core/Classes/DataHandling/DataHandler.php:3252 (cmdmap copy) and 3491-3493 (copyRecord re-submits through a local DataHandler)
traps.type: how-type (M6: a producer on a nested path the outer check never sees)
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream core code: the copy command inserts a fresh row by re-submitting it through a second DataHandler instance with an internally generated identifier, so a fix that guards only the caller's own datamap/cmdmap surface, or that trusts internal maintenance instances, leaves the duplicate open while every other route is closed
